 1         Plaintiff TOP GAMING NETWORK LTD. (“Plaintiff” or “TGN”) alleges the
 2   following against Defendant DOUBLE COCONUT LLC (“Defendant” or “Double
 3   Coconut”):
 4                               NATURE OF THE ACTION
 5         1.      This action arises from a material breach of a Work For Hire Master
 6   Services Agreement by Defendant, a software developer, who failed to deliver a
 7   functional video game per the agreed-upon milestones. Plaintiff, having paid

 8   Defendant for work that was never properly completed, seeks to recover its property,

 9   the “Work Product,” including all source code and assets, and to be compensated for

10   the damages it has suffered as a result of Defendant’s failures.

11
                                         THE PARTIES

12
           2.      Plaintiff TOP GAMING NETWORK LTD. is a corporation organized
     and existing under the laws of Malta, with its principal place of business at Level
13
     3A/4A 240 Msida Road, Gzira, Malta.
14
           3.      Plaintiff is informed and believes, and on that basis alleges, that
15
     Defendant DOUBLE COCONUT LLC is a limited liability company organized and
16
     existing under the laws of the State of California, with its principal place of business
17
     at 1583 33rd Ave., San Francisco, CA 94122. Plaintiff is further informed and
18
     believes that all members of Double Coconut LLC are citizens of the State of
19
     California.
20
                                JURISDICTION AND VENUE
21
           4.      This Court has subject matter jurisdiction over this action pursuant to
22
     28 U.S.C. § 1332(a)(2) because this is a civil action between a citizen of a foreign
23
     state and a citizen of the State of California, and the matter in controversy exceeds
24
     the sum or value of $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs.
25
           5.      This Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendant because Defendant
26
     is domiciled in this District and its principal place of business is in this District.
27

28

                                                 1
                                             COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK      Document 1     Filed 12/08/25    Page 3 of 10


 1         6.     Venue is proper in this District under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1) and (b)(2)
 2   because Defendant resides in this District and a substantial part of the events or
 3   omissions giving rise to the claims occurred in this District.
 4         7.     Additionally, venue is mandatory in this District pursuant to a forum
 5   selection clause in the parties’ agreement, which states: “Each Party shall bring any
 6   suit, action or other proceeding with respect to the Agreement in a Federal District
 7   Court located in San Francisco County, San Francisco, CA.”

 8                                          FACTS

 9         A. The Master Services Agreement (MSA)

10         8.     On or about October 1, 2024, Plaintiff and Defendant entered into a

11
     written contract titled “Work For Hire Master Services Agreement” (the “MSA”). A

12
     true and correct copy of the MSA is attached hereto as Exhibit 1 and incorporated
     by reference.
13
           9.     Pursuant to the MSA and its “Exhibit A, Statement of Work #1” (the
14
     “SOW”), Defendant agreed to develop a front-end video slot game for Plaintiff titled
15
     “Cha Cha Bomb” (the “Game”).
16
           10.    The MSA is a work for hire agreement. Under the Proprietary Rights
17
     section, the parties explicitly agreed that all Work Product, which includes all
18
     “technical information, computer or other specifications, documentation, works of
19
     authorship... ideas, knowledge, or data... originated by Contractor,” would be the
20
     exclusive property of TGN.
21
           11.    The MSA states: “Company shall own all right, title and interest in and
22
     to the Work Product created hereunder . . . Contractor expressly acknowledges that
23
     the Parties have agreed that all aspects of the Work Product... are to be considered
24
     ‘works made for hire’ . . . and that Company is to be the ‘author[.]’”
25
           12.    The SOW established a milestone-based development plan and
26
     payment schedule, which included an “Alpha” milestone and a “Beta” milestone.
27
           13.    TGN performed all, or substantially all, of its obligations under the
28
     MSA, including making timely payments to Defendant for the Kick-Off, Pre-
                                               2
                                           COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK         Document 1     Filed 12/08/25   Page 4 of 10


 1   Production, Alpha, and Beta milestones, and providing Defendant with a fully
 2   working backend, API documentation, and continuous technical support and
 3   clarification.
 4          B. Defendant’s Material Breach of the MSA
 5          14.       Beginning in or around late 2024 and continuing through July 2025,
 6   Defendant materially breached the MSA and SOW by, among other things:
 7                    a. Failing to deliver a functional “Alpha” build that met the SOW

 8                       requirements;

 9                    b. Failing to deliver a “Beta” build that incorporated the “must-have”

10                       features essential to the Game’s design, despite TGN having paid

11
                         Defendant for the Beta milestone;

12
                      c. Consistently delivering builds that were plagued with fundamental
                         bugs and defects, such as “black screen” errors on mobile devices,
13
                         rendering them unusable for testing or review;
14
                      d. Failing to implement critical “must-have” features that were
15
                         communicated to Defendant from the project’s inception, including
16
                         seamless user interaction, animation skip functions, and a consistent
17
                         User Interface;
18
                      e. Unilaterally and improperly attempting to re-scope the project and
19
                         deem it in a “polish period” when, in fact, the core “Alpha” and
20
                         “Beta” functionalities had not been delivered; and
21
                      f. Failing to meet the agreed-upon project timelines, causing
22
                         significant delays to TGN's business plans.
23
            15.       On information and belief, Defendant also breached the MSA by
24
     incorporating third-party copyrighted materials into the deliverables without
25
     authorization, exposing TGN to legal liability.
26
            16.       Although TGN paid Defendant’s invoice for the “Beta” milestone,
27
     TGN did so in a good-faith effort to accelerate progress. TGN never formally
28

                                                  3
                                              COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK        Document 1   Filed 12/08/25   Page 5 of 10


 1   approved or accepted the Beta milestone, as the build delivered by Defendant was
 2   non-functional and incomplete.
 3         C. TGN Terminates the MSA and Demands Its Property
 4         17.    Based on Defendant’s persistent and incurable material breaches, TGN,
 5   through its legal counsel, notified Defendant in writing on or about July 15, 2025,
 6   and again on July 24, 2025, that TGN considered the MSA terminated effective
 7   immediately.

 8         18.    The “Term and Termination” provision of the MSA provides that upon

 9   termination, Defendant: “must deliver to the Company, within 10 days of the

10   termination, all Work Product, any work-in-progress and any other materials related

11
     to the development and performance of the Services if such Work Product and

12
     materials have been paid for.”
           19.    TGN has paid for all Work Product created by Defendant through at
13
     least the Beta milestone.
14
           20.    On July 15, 2025, July 24, 2025, and again on August 4, 2025, TGN
15
     demanded that Defendant comply with its contractual obligation to deliver all Work
16
     Product that had been paid for, including all source code, build files, documentation,
17
     and art assets.
18
           21.    Defendant has failed and refused, and continues to fail and refuse, to
19
     deliver the Work Product to TGN.
20
           22.    Defendant is in wrongful possession of TGN’s property, which TGN
21
     paid for and owns outright under the “work for hire” provisions of the MSA.
22
           23.    As a direct and proximate result of Defendant’s breaches and wrongful
23
     withholding of the Work Product, TGN has been significantly damaged. It has been
24
     forced to scrap its development timeline, cannot use a different developer to finish
25
     the Game without the source code it already paid for, and has lost the entire benefit
26
     of its bargain, all while Defendant holds TGN's property hostage.
27
                                  FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION
28
                                 (Breach of Contract - Damages)
                                               4
                                           COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK      Document 1     Filed 12/08/25   Page 6 of 10


 1                                (Against All Defendants)
 2         24.    TGN re-alleges and incorporates by reference each allegation contained
 3   in paragraphs 1 through 23, inclusive, as though fully set forth herein.
 4         25.    The MSA is a valid and enforceable contract between TGN and
 5   Defendant.
 6         26.    TGN performed all, or substantially all, of the conditions, covenants,
 7   and promises required on its part to be performed in accordance with the terms of

 8   the MSA, or its performance was excused by Defendant’s breaches.

 9         27.    Defendant materially breached the terms of the MSA, including by

10   failing to deliver functional and complete “Alpha” and “Beta” milestone builds,

11
     failing to adhere to the project's core requirements, and, following termination,

12
     failing to deliver the paid-for Work Product as required by the MSA’s termination
     clause.
13
           28.    As a direct and proximate result of Defendant’s breaches, TGN has
14
     sustained, and will continue to sustain, damages in an amount to be proven at trial.
15
     These damages include, but are not limited to, all payments made to Defendant for
16
     which TGN received no value, the cost of hiring a new developer to complete or re-
17
     create the Game (cost-to-cover), and lost profits from TGN's inability to launch the
18
     Game as scheduled.
19
                              SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION
20
        (Specific Performance of Contractual Obligation – In the Alternative to
21
                                     Breach of Contract)
22
                                  (Against All Defendants)
23
           29.    TGN re-alleges and incorporates by reference each allegation contained
24
     in paragraphs 1 through 23, inclusive, as though fully set forth herein.
25
           30.    This cause of action is pled in the alternative to the First Cause of
26
     Action.
27
           31.    The MSA contains a specific, post-termination covenant requiring
28
     Defendant to “deliver to the Company, within 10 days of the termination, all Work
                                               5
                                           COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK      Document 1     Filed 12/08/25    Page 7 of 10


 1   Product, any work-in-progress . . . if such Work Product and materials have been
 2   paid for.”
 3          32.   TGN has paid for the Work Product through at least the Beta milestone.
 4   Defendant's obligation to deliver this Work Product is clear and definite.
 5          33.   TGN has demanded that Defendant perform this obligation, and
 6   Defendant has refused.
 7          34.   TGN has no adequate remedy at law. The Work Product, which

 8   includes all source code, proprietary logic, and custom art assets for the Game, is

 9   unique. Monetary damages are insufficient to compensate TGN for the loss of this

10   unique Work Product, which TGN owns as a “work for hire” and which represents

11
     many months of development, feedback, and investment. TGN cannot be made

12
     whole without the delivery of the specific Work Product it paid for.
            35.   TGN therefore requests, in the alternative to general damages, a
13
     judgment for specific performance compelling Defendant to immediately deliver to
14
     TGN all Work Product, in all formats, including but not limited to all source code,
15
     build files, documentation, and art and animation assets.
16
                               THIRD CAUSE OF ACTION
17
                       (Declaratory Relief - 28 U.S.C. §§ 2201, 2202)
18
                                  (Against All Defendants)
19
            36.   TGN re-alleges and incorporates by reference each allegation contained
20
     in paragraphs 1 through 23, inclusive, as though fully set forth herein.
21
            37.   An actual and justiciable controversy has arisen and now exists between
22
     TGN and Defendant concerning their respective rights and obligations under the
23
     MSA.
24
            38.   TGN contends that (a) Defendant materially breached the MSA; (b)
25
     TGN’s termination of the MSA was proper and effective; (c) all Work Product
26
     created by Defendant under the MSA is the sole and exclusive property of TGN as
27
     a “work for hire”; and (d) TGN is entitled to the immediate possession of all Work
28
     Product for which it has paid.
                                               6
                                           COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK      Document 1     Filed 12/08/25   Page 8 of 10


 1         39.    Plaintiff is informed and believes that Defendant disputes these
 2   contentions and wrongfully asserts a right to withhold the Work Product from TGN.
 3         40.    TGN desires a judicial determination and declaration of its rights and
 4   Defendant’s obligations. A declaration from this Court is necessary and appropriate
 5   to resolve the parties’ dispute regarding ownership and possession of the Work
 6   Product.
 7         41.    TGN therefore seeks a declaratory judgment from this Court that:

 8                a. Defendant materially breached the MSA;

 9                b. TGN’s termination of the MSA was valid;

10                c. TGN is the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest

11
                     in and to all Work Product created by Defendant pursuant to the

12
                     MSA; and
                  d. TGN is entitled to immediate possession of all Work Product for
13
                     which it has paid.
14
                              FOURTH CAUSE OF ACTION
15
                 (Conversion - In the Alternative to Breach of Contract)
16
           42.    TGN re-alleges and incorporates by reference each allegation contained
17
     in paragraphs 1 through 23, inclusive, as though fully set forth herein.
18
           43.    This cause of action is pled in the alternative to the First Cause of
19
     Action.
20
           44.    At all relevant times, TGN was, and is, the owner and has a right to
21
     immediate possession of the Work Product, including all source code, assets, and
22
     documentation related to the “Cha Cha Bomb” game. TGN’s ownership is
23
     established by the “work for hire” provision of the MSA and its payments to
24
     Defendant for the creation of said Work Product.
25
           45.    TGN made multiple written demands upon Defendant for the return of
26
     its property, the Work Product, including on July 15, July 24, and August 4, 2025.
27
           46.    Defendant has failed and refused, and continues to fail and refuse, to
28
     return the Work Product to TGN.
                                               7
                                           COMPLAINT
      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK        Document 1    Filed 12/08/25   Page 9 of 10


 1         47.     By wrongfully withholding and refusing to turn over the Work Product,
 2   Defendant has intentionally and substantially interfered with TGN’s property rights.
 3         48.     As a direct and proximate result of Defendant's conversion, TGN has
 4   been damaged in an amount to be proven at trial.
 5         49.     Furthermore, because Defendant’s conduct was willful, malicious, and
 6   oppressive, and in conscious disregard of TGN's property rights, TGN is entitled to
 7   an award of punitive damages.

 8                                      PRAYER FOR RELIEF

 9         WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment against Defendant as follows:

10         (i)     As to the First Cause of Action for Breach of Contract, Plaintiff prays

11
                   for general, special, and consequential damages in an amount according

12
                   to proof at trial.
           (ii)    In the Alternative, as to the Second Cause of Action for Specific
13
                   Performance, Plaintiff prays for an order of specific performance
14
                   compelling Defendant, its officers, agents, and employees to
15
                   immediately deliver to TGN all Work Product, in native and all other
16
                   formats, including but not limited to all source code, build files,
17
                   documentation, and art and animation assets related to the “Cha Cha
18
                   Bomb” game.
19
           (iii)   As to the Third Cause of Action for Declaratory Relief, Plaintiff prays
20
                   for a declaratory judgment that: (a) Defendant materially breached the
21
                   MSA; (b) TGN’s termination of the MSA was valid; (c) TGN is the
22
                   sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all
23
                   Work Product created by Defendant pursuant to the MSA; and (d) TGN
24
                   is entitled to immediate possession of all Work Product for which it has
25
                   paid.
26
           (iv)    In the Alternative, as to the Fourth Cause of Action for Conversion,
27
                   Plaintiff prays for: (a) damages according to proof at trial for the value
28
                   of the converted property; (b) for an order compelling the return of the
                                                8

      Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK    Document 1      Filed 12/08/25   Page 10 of 10


 1              Work Product; and (c) for punitive and exemplary damages in an
 2              amount sufficient to punish and deter Defendant’s wrongful conduct.
 3        (v)   As to all Causes of Action, Plaintiff prays for: (a) pre-judgment and
 4              post-judgment interest at the maximum legal rate; (b) for costs of suit
 5              incurred herein; and (c) for such other and further relief as the Court
 6              may deem just and proper.
 7                           DEMAND FOR JURY TRIAL

 8        Plaintiff hereby demands a trial by jury on all issues so triable.

                             Work For Hire
                       Master Services Agreement


This document dated October 1, 2024 shall confirm the agreement
between TOP Gaming Network Ltd. (the “Company”) located at Level
3A/4A 240 Msida Road, Gzira, Malta and Double Coconut LLC located
at 1583 33rd Ave., San Francisco, CA 94122 USA (hereinafter referred
to as “Contractor”) pursuant to which Contractor will serve as a
contractor to the Company (the “Agreement”).

The parties mentioned above will be referred individually to as “Party“
and collectively referred to as “Parties“.

The terms of this Agreement are as follows:
Services
Contractor’s initial responsibilities will be according to Exhibit A (the
“Initial Responsibilities”).
Additional responsibilities must be agreed to, signed, and dated by
both Contractor and the Company in additional Statements of Work
(each a “Statement of Work” or “SOW”), and shall be subject to the
terms and conditions set forth herein, unless an individual Statement
of Work expressly and specifically notes that there is a deviation from
the terms of this Agreement for the purposes of such Statement of
Work.

Fees
Fees shall be either based on a daily Time and Materials allocation
basis, per the rate sheet indicated in Exhibit A, or shall be based on
milestone delivery basis per any future Statements of Work. For
Additional Responsibilities or Roles, if any, requested by the Company,
fees shall be mutually agreed by the Parties and shall be mentioned in
an additional Rate Sheet.

                                                                            1
Double Coconut MSA
   Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK    Document 1-1   Filed 12/08/25   Page 3 of 20




For Time and Materials billing, Contractor will invoice the Company on
the first day of every month for hours worked in the previous month,
as well as any agreed Reimbursable Expenses.
For Milestone billing, Contractor will invoice the Company upon
approval of any milestone as well as any agreed Reimbursable
Expenses.

Company will remit payment within 15 business days of receipt of
invoice via check or bank wire. Credit card payments are also
acceptable but require an additional 3% processing fee.
Cryptocurrency payments are available as well upon written approval
by both parties. A late fee of 2% per month shall apply and accrue if
payment is late.

Status
Contractor will serve as an independent contractor to the Company.
Contractor, Contractor’s employees, subcontractors or subcontractor’s
employees are not, and shall not be deemed to be, employees of the
Company. Neither Contractor nor any of Contractor’s employees or
subcontractors will represent to any third party that he or she is an
officer or employee of the Company, nor shall enter into any
agreement involving the Company, incur any obligations on the
Company’s behalf, or commit the Company in any manner without the
Company’s prior consent. As an independent contractor, Contractor
will be responsible for all withholding taxes, social security,
unemployment or disability insurance benefits or similar items, and/or
other amounts due arising out of independent contractor and/or
consultant status, including any such amounts owed with respect to its
employees and subcontractors. In addition, as an independent
contractor, neither Contractor nor any of Contractor’s employees or
subcontractors are eligible for any employee benefit programs from
the Company.
The Agreement (including the Statements of Work) shall not be
construed as constituting either Party as partner, joint venture or
                                                                          2
Double Coconut MSA
    Case 3:25-cv-10509-SK    Document 1-1   Filed 12/08/25   Page 4 of 20




fiduciary of the other Party or to create any other form of legal
association that would impose liability upon one Party for the act or
failure to act of the other Party, or as providing either Party with the
right, power or authority (express or implied) to create any duty or
obligation of the other Party.

Non-solicitation

From the date of this Agreement until 24 months after the termination
of this Agreement (the “Restricted Period”), Contractor will not,
without the Company’s prior written consent, directly or indirectly,
solicit or encourage any employee or contractor of the Company or its
affiliates to terminate employment with, or cease providing services
to, the Company or its affiliates. Additionally, during the Restricted
Period, Company will not, without the Contractor’s prior written
consent, directly or indirectly, solicit or encourage any employee or
contractor of the Contractor or its affiliates to terminate employment
with, or cease providing services to, the Contractor or its affiliates.

Term and Termination
Engagement of Contractor’s Initial Responsibilities will commence
upon the date specific in this Agreement (the “Effective Date”), as
identified below.
Responsibilities will continue until this Agreement is terminated by
either party.
The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately by written
notice for cause for the following circumstances: (i) material breach of
this Agreement or any SOW; (ii) violation of any third party intellectual
property in the course of performance of services under this
Agreement or any SOW (iii) termination in accordance with the
Regulatory Compliance section below, (iv) dishonesty, fraud,
misrepresentation, criminal conduct or failure or inability with respect
to the entering into and/or the performance of this Agreement; or (v)

                                                                           3

circumstances causing the Company to believe, in good faith, that
Contractor or any of Contractor’s owners, directors, employees, or
Service Providers has engaged in material illegal conduct or unethical
business practices, including any Improper Conduct, or any violations
of any applicable laws, including Anti-Corruption Laws, Rules, and
Regulations, directly or indirectly, in connection with performance of
this Agreement. The Company will not be liable for any claims, losses,
or damages arising from or related to failure by Contractor to comply
with any applicable laws, including Anti-Corruption Laws, Rules, and
Regulations, or this Agreement or related to the termination of this
Agreement under this clause, and Contractor will indemnify and hold
the Company harmless against any such claims, losses, or damages.

Contractor or the Company may terminate this Agreement for
convenience with 30 days notice.
In the event the Company terminates the Agreement for convenience,
any earned but unpaid fees up until and including the next 30 days

                             Statement of Work #1

Cha Cha Bomb is a fruit-style themed slot game for the Italian market,
themed for Cuban dance with a special scatter free spin feature, a wild bomb
symbol that becomes a “sticky symbol”, and the ability for players to choose
their own sticky symbol. There is also a progress meter leading to the bonus
wild.




An additional special feature of the game is the ability to provide a really
smooth user experience where the player can skip or fast-forward everything
and immediately experience the next spin.

The game will also have a special “QA Panel” so all features can be tested
easily:
